chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding the man who prays, and in front of him is a Mushaf (Quran) open, in his Qiblah, he said: 'No.' I said, 'And if it is in a wrapping?' He said: 'Yes.'
And he said: 'The man cannot pray, and in his Qiblah is a fire, or iron.'

And regarding the man who prays, and in front of him is a hanging lantern and in it is fire, except that it is towards him. He said: 'When it is high, it would be evil. One should not pray towards it.'

key_terms.بِحِيَالِهِ: Facing him / in front of him
key_terms.مُصْحَفٌ: A codex or copy of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What objects in front of a worshipper invalidate or make prayer disliked in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the juristic nuances of the 'sutra' (prayer screen) concept, distinguishing between objects that invalidate prayer when placed directly in the Qiblah line, such as an open Quran, fire, or iron, and those that are merely disliked, like a high-hanging lantern. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on minimizing distractions and maintaining reverence during prayer, while allowing flexibility for wrapped scriptures. The ruling underscores the importance of visual focus (khushu) by removing potential obstructions or sources of distraction from the direct line of sight toward the Kaaba.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Imran Bin Musa, and Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddiq Bin Sadaqa, from Ammar Al Sabaty, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said regarding the man who prays, and in front of him is a Parchment (Holy Quran), open, in his Qiblah, said: ‘No’. I said, ‘Supposing it was in a wrapping?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
And heasws said: ‘The man cannot pray Salāt and in his Qiblah is a fire, or iron’.

And about the man who prays, and in front of him is a hanging lantern and in it is fire, except that it is towards him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it is high, it would be evil. One should not pray towards it’.
en.sarwar: 15. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Imran ibn Musa and Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ali from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar al-Sabatiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs Salah (prayer) and in front of him there is an open copy of Quran. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not permissible.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if it is in a cover?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is permissible.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘One is not to perform Salah (prayer) with a fire in front of him, or iron.’

He (the Imam) was asked about a man who performs Salah (prayer) with a chandelier hanging in his front with fire in it except that it is his view. He (the Imam) said, ‘When it is higher it is evil. One is not to perform Salah (prayer) with it in one’s view.’”
